# A binary secret changed on both sides cannot be line-merged. The driver must
# detect the binary content (NUL byte), refuse the text merge, and write both
# decrypted sides next to the revealed file for manual resolution - never corrupt
# the object or empty the revealed file.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# A binary secret (contains a NUL byte), shared base.
exec sh -c 'printf "head\000BASE\n" > blob.bin'
exec sesam add blob.bin --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add binary secret'

# OURS and THEIRS change the binary content differently.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sh -c 'printf "head\000OURS\n" > blob.bin'
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sh -c 'printf "head\000THEIRS\n" > blob.bin'
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs'

# Merge: binary detected -> both sides written out, revealed kept as ours.
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stderr 'binary secret blob.bin changed on both sides'
exists blob.bin.ours
exists blob.bin.theirs
grep 'OURS' blob.bin
! grep 'THEIRS' blob.bin

# sesam status surfaces the binary conflict on the parent secret (even without
# --all) and does not list the .ours/.theirs side files as their own entries.
exec sesam status
stdout 'blob.bin'
stdout 'conflicted'
! stdout 'blob.bin.ours'
! stdout 'blob.bin.theirs'

# Finalizing while the side files remain is refused - a binary conflict has no
# in-file markers, so the pre-commit gate keys on the leftover .ours/.theirs.
exec git add -A
! exec git commit --no-edit
stderr 'unresolved merge conflicts'
stderr 'blob.bin.*binary'

# Resolve by taking theirs, drop the side files, finalize.
exec sh -c 'cp blob.bin.theirs blob.bin'
exec rm blob.bin.ours blob.bin.theirs
exec git add -A
exec git commit --no-edit

exec sesam verify
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/blob.bin.sesam
stdout 'THEIRS'
